thread.title_full: Tri-Cities air quality worsens as wildfires swell in OR, WA - NewsBreak

author: Eric Rosane
title: Tri-Cities air quality worsens as wildfires swell in OR, WA - NewsBreak
text:
By Eric Rosane ,
3 hours ago
Air quality in Kennewick dipped into “unhealthy” territory for sensitive groups Wednesday afternoon as regional wildfires in Oregon and Central Washington continue to choke the Tri-Cities.
The city’s air quality index rose past 100 by 3 p.m., according to sensor data provided by the Washington Department of Ecology.
It’s recommended residents keep outdoor activities light and short, and for those with sensitive heart or lung diseases, older adults, children and pregnant women to go indoors if they have symptoms.
Air quality around the rest of the Tri-Cities remained “moderate,” according to Ecology officials. Most people are OK to go outside, but sensitive individuals should keep outdoor activities “light and short.”
The Emigrant Fire, in south-central Oregon, has burned more than 26,000 acres since it was started by lightning on Aug. 24. It is 0% contained, with more than 1,100 firefighters working it, according to the Northwest Interagency Coordination Center .
The smoke is creating some spectacular sunrises over the cable bridge on the Columbia River in the Tri-Cities. Laurie Williams/Tri-City Herald Several other wildfires in the Washington range of the Cascade Mountains and in Eastern Washington have scorched an additional 10,000 acres and continue to be a hazardous.
Ecology and the Yakima Regional Clear Air Agency has issued air quality alerts for most of Central Washington due to smoke caused by current and expected regional wildfires.
“When air quality is unhealthy, everyone should reduce exposure,” NWS says.
“Limit time outside, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips for cleaner indoor air. Hot temperatures will increase the risk of heat-related illnesses. Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors,” the agency advised.
The hot temperatures even have squirrels “splooting” to try and cool off in Kennewick. Courtesy Lori Cannard Much of the Mid-Columbia and beyond — from Wenatchee to Lewiston and down to The Dalles — remains under an extreme heat warning issued by the National Weather Service in Pendleton .
Expect subtle but widespread haze, and temperatures in the high 90s throughout the rest of the week in the Tri-Cities .
The weather service forecasts a reprieve next week — high temperatures in the 70s and 80s with a chance of showers.
